about: The one source of Lumen's Content-Security-Policy and security headers. Edit this file, then run `npm run headers:write` (rewrites the policy values in every file listed under `sources`) and commit both. `npm run headers` (CI) fails when any source differs. Why each value is what it is: docs/security/headers.md.

app.why: The editor: index.html and every SPA route. No eval on the page (Graphviz, ruby.wasm and the TypeScript checker run in workers with their own policy); WebAssembly compiles ('wasm-unsafe-eval'). Trusted Types guard every DOM sink (src/lib/trustedTypes.ts).

playground-runner.why: Web Playground runner: the page inside the playground block's sandboxed iframe (sandbox="allow-scripts", opaque origin). Runs the user's own project: blob: modules (the linked project files) and eval (Vue's template compiler); framed by the app only.

livejs-runner.why: live-js runner (T48): hidden sandboxed iframe (opaque origin). The user's code runs in a blob: worker that inherits this policy: eval for the code itself and no network at all. The fixed public nonce is for WebKit, which does not match 'self' in an opaque-origin frame (vite.config.ts html.cspNonce adds it to the page's script tags).

tesseract.why: On-device OCR (T31): the tesseract.js worker and its wasm cores. A dedicated worker takes the policy of its own response; the app's Trusted Types requirement would block the worker's importScripts() of the core. Language models come from raw.githubusercontent.com on first use.

eval-workers.why: Worker scripts that need eval, each served with its own policy so the page allows none: Graphviz (Emscripten embind builds its bindings with new Function), ruby.wasm, the TypeScript checker, and webR's worker under /webr/ (R.js evaluates EM_ASM code of side modules and webr::eval_js with eval). Their network is the app's own origin only.

X-Frame-Options.why: Legacy twin of frame-ancestors 'none'. Nothing frames the app; the two runner pages are framed by the app and must not carry it (they use frame-ancestors 'self').

Permissions-Policy.why: Microphone for dictation and voice memos (getUserMedia({ audio: true }) in src/ui/VoiceDictation.tsx). Nothing in the app uses the camera or geolocation, so both are off.

Strict-Transport-Security.why: Only the managed HTTPS hosts send it. The nginx images listen on plain HTTP behind the operator's TLS terminator; includeSubDomains + preload on someone else's domain is their decision.

Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy.why: Only the root Dockerfile image (deploy/nginx.conf) opts into cross-origin isolation (multi-threaded WebAssembly). See docs/security/headers.md for its cost.

Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy.why: Pairs with Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy on the deploy image; every document and worker it serves carries it so nested frames and workers stay loadable.

cloudflare.why: public/_headers: Cloudflare Pages (and Netlify, which applies dist/_headers but cannot detach headers). The build copies it to dist/_headers and adds the deployment's endpoint origins to every connect-src (src/build/cspEndpoints.ts).

docker-nginx.why: docker/nginx.conf: the on-prem web shell (docker/Dockerfile.web, docker-compose.yml).

csp.why: Placeholder that docker/Dockerfile.web replaces with the deployment's endpoint origins (dist/.csp-connect-extra, written by the Vite CSP plugin).

deploy-nginx.why: deploy/nginx.conf + deploy/lumen-runtime-headers.conf: the root Dockerfile image (fly.toml).

csp.why: Placeholder that the root Dockerfile replaces with the deployment's endpoint origins (dist/.csp-connect-extra, written by the Vite CSP plugin). Without it the header, enforced next to the meta CSP, blocks the configured endpoints.

meta.why: <meta http-equiv> copies in the HTML pages. They also cover the contexts that send no header (Vite dev, Tauri, Capacitor) and are enforced next to the header everywhere else.

csp.why: Ignored in <meta> (CSP3); browsers log an error for it.
Trusted Types are enforced by the production response headers only; the dev server, Tauri and Capacitor webviews have not been verified under them.

tauri.why: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json app.security.csp. Tauri sends it only with .html assets (tauri crate: manager get_asset), so workers keep their own needs; index.html's meta policy is enforced next to it.

csp.why: A top-level desktop window is never framed (and on Linux Tauri injects the policy as <meta>); Trusted Types as for meta.

ipc: / http://ipc.localhost are Tauri 2's IPC protocol (macOS and Linux / Windows). https: because this policy is compiled from tauri.conf.json and cannot receive the deployment's endpoint origins at build time; the meta policy, which does, still holds the page to the explicit list.
